[happy] The audit view header keeps every main tab visible and the .tools group right of them at any viewport the chrome supports: the tablist and .tools cannot shrink below their intrinsic width (flex-shrink: 0) and .product carries the shrink budget via min-width: 0 (both on the flex item and on .product .name) so the project name ellipsizes first.

[happy] The .product .name span carries a title="<full name>" attribute so hovering reveals the whole name when the ellipsis has clipped it; the title is HTML-escaped on the same path as the inner text, and when the product block collapses (no project name on the tree) no title attribute is emitted.

[happy] The header display name prefers prd.productName, then manifest.projectName, then prd.productTitle. A rename via `rcf define update PRD-001 --set productName=...` therefore reaches the audit chrome without touching manifest.projectName (which the chain keeps for ids and paths).
View freshness
An edit on disk is present after the view is regenerated
The view is produced fresh from the on-disk tree and carries no cached prior state
Build/DAG sub-tab: layout, closure, inspector, deep links, filters, cycles, no outbound postMessage

[happy] Given the Build tab's DAG sub-tab, when it renders, then every connected FBS sits in a column whose index equals its longest dependency depth from `dependsOnFbsIds` (0 for no dependency) and rows inside a column are ordered by `buildOrder` ascending.

[happy] Given the DAG canvas, when a node is clicked, then it is selected, its upstream closure outlines in the link colour and its downstream closure outlines in the warning colour; a second click on the same node clears the selection.

[happy] Given a selected FBS, when the inspector renders, then it lists status, area, AC count, size, build order, a buildable-now flag, direct and transitive needs, direct and transitive waits-on and an "Open in Specs" link that moves to `#tab=build&sub=specs&entity=<id>`.

[happy] Given a selection, when it is set or cleared, then the hash becomes `#tab=build&sub=dag&entity=<id>` (or drops the entity key when cleared) and a reload with that hash restores the selection and scrolls the node into view.
[happy] Given the DAG toolbar, when the Status, Area, Buildable-now, Critical-path or Show-unconnected filter changes, then the visible nodes update and the current selection is kept.
[failure] Given a `dependsOnFbsIds` cycle on disk, when the DAG renders, then the cycle is reported as a finding in the toolbar area and the remaining non-cycle FBS still render.
[must-not] Given the DAG canvas, when a node is clicked, filtered or inspected, then no `postMessage` is sent to the parent window and no outbound network request is made.
ID lookup: ranking, hash pick, embed/theme round-trip, empty state, no outbound side effects

[happy] Given the review surface, when the SearchButton is pressed or Cmd/Ctrl+F is typed from any tab, then the LookupModal opens; typing an exact id (`REQ-002`) or a prefix (`REQ-00`) ranks that id first and the first result row is pre-highlighted.
[happy] Given the LookupModal, when a word query matches a document's title and another document's snippet, then the title match ranks above the snippet match.
[happy] Given the LookupModal, when a query of exactly one character is typed, then only ids whose identifier contains that character rank, and the title / snippet word-match pass is skipped.

[happy] Given a pre-highlighted result for `US-304`, when Enter is pressed, then the hash becomes `#tab=requirements&entity=US-304`, the Router activates the Requirements tab, opens the REQ-003 ancestor DocRow and the US-304 row, scrolls the target into view and flashes it.

[happy] Given a mount URL `?tab=requirements&entity=US-304`, when the shell first paints, then the Router lands on the same position: Requirements tab active, REQ-003 and US-304 DocRows open, US-304 scrolled into view.

[happy] Given `?embed=1&theme=dark` on the viewer URL, when a result is picked from the LookupModal, then the resulting URL still carries `embed=1` and `theme=dark` in the query string and the hash is `#tab=<tab>&entity=<id>`.

[failure] Given a `./index.json` fetch that returns a non-2xx status or a malformed body, when the LookupModal is opened, then an empty state renders with a reload affordance that re-fetches the index, and no result rows show.

[must-not] Given the LookupModal, when the user types a query, picks a result or closes the modal, then no `postMessage` is sent to the parent window, no outbound network request beyond the `./index.json` fetch is made, and no search term is written to `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / cookies.

[happy] Given the SearchButton (`.rcf-search-btn`) in the shell's `.tools` group, when it is rendered in either theme and in each of its states (default, `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`), then the computed foreground / background contrast ratio for the button text, the icon stroke against the background and the focus-ring colour against the adjacent surface meets WCAG 2.1 AA (>= 4.5:1 for the text, >= 3:1 for the icon and the focus-ring boundary) in both the light (`:root`) and dark (`:root[data-theme="dark"]`) token sets.
Wespa host fixture: iframe shell, theme postMessage, hash-nav embed preservation, cross-origin refusal, three lints, no new outbound postMessage shape

[happy] Given the test-host fixture at `/test-host.html`, when the page loads with the viewer served from the same origin, then the iframe `src` is `./?embed=1&theme=light`, the title block and footer of the iframed viewer are hidden (`<html data-embed="1">`), the tab nav is visible and the host's 56px header plus the resizable sidebar render around it.

[happy] Given the test-host fixture with the iframe loaded, when the host's theme toggle posts `{ type: "rcf-view-theme", theme: "dark" }` to the iframe's `contentWindow`, then the iframe's `<html data-theme>` flips to `dark` without a reload and the content repaints in the dark token set.

[happy] Given the test-host fixture with the iframe loaded at `./?embed=1&theme=dark`, when a hash-only navigation inside the iframe writes `#tab=requirements&entity=REQ-002`, then the iframe's query still carries `embed=1` and `theme=dark` and the viewer's inner `<html data-embed="1" data-theme="dark">` is preserved.

[failure] Given the viewer page listening for `rcf-view-theme` postMessages, when a message with `event.origin` different from `window.location.origin` is delivered, then the message is ignored and `<html data-theme>` is not changed.

[must-not] Given the viewer's `GET /` response, when the three lints run in the test suite, then (a) no `X-Frame-Options` header is set and no CSP `frame-ancestors` directive forbids same-origin framing, (b) `target="_top"` appears zero times in the rendered HTML across every tab, (c) every `localStorage.{setItem,getItem,removeItem}` and shared `storage.*` call site under `src/view/**` uses a key starting with `rcf-view:v1:`.

[must-not] Given the test-host fixture and the viewer page, when either is loaded, then neither posts any outbound message beyond the host's `rcf-view-theme`; the viewer sends no `postMessage` of any shape, and the test-host adds no new postMessage shape.

[happy] Given the standalone viewer loaded without `embed=1`, when the shell paints, then a three-state theme control (`role="group"`, three buttons Light|Dark|Auto with `aria-pressed`) renders in the header's `.tools` group right of the SearchButton; when a button is pressed, `<html data-theme>` is set to `light` or `dark` (or the attribute is removed for Auto so the `prefers-color-scheme` media query decides) live without a reload, and the pressed button's `aria-pressed` becomes `true` while the others become `false`.

[happy] Given the standalone (non-embed) viewer, when a theme button is pressed, then the chosen value (`light`, `dark` or `auto`) is written to `localStorage['rcf-view:v1:theme']`; on the next page load the stored value is reapplied; the boot precedence is `?theme=` wins first, then the stored value, then the default (`auto`); and the postMessage `rcf-view-theme` listener still applies live but writes nothing to the stored key.

[must-not] Given the viewer loaded with `?embed=1`, when the shell paints, then the three-state theme control is absent from the DOM entirely (no `[data-rcf-theme-control]` element rendered, not merely hidden by CSS), and no read or write of `localStorage['rcf-view:v1:theme']` happens on load, on a postMessage theme change, or on any user action inside the viewer.

[happy] Given the standalone viewer with a stored value `rcf-view:v1:theme = dark`, when the URL carries `?theme=light`, then on load `<html data-theme>` is `light` (the explicit query wins) and the Light button is pressed; the stored value is left as `dark` and is reused on the next load without a `?theme=` query.
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast audit across the viewer stylesheet, both themes, every state

[happy] Given the viewer stylesheet `src/view/style.css` and the two token blocks (`:root` and `:root[data-theme="dark"]`), when the contrast test runs, then it enumerates every CSS rule that sets `color` (and every state rule merged over its base selector, so a state that changes only the background is paired with the inherited colour) paired with every reachable background (own rule, nearest ancestor surface token, page background `--sv-canvas`) and every state variant (default, `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, `[aria-pressed="true"]`, `[aria-selected="true"]`, `.is-active`, `:disabled`), computes the WCAG relative-luminance contrast ratio for each, and asserts >= 4.5:1 for text, >= 3:1 for large text (>= 18.66px bold or >= 24px) and for non-text UI boundaries (control borders and outlines, focus rings against the adjacent colour, each enumerated as its own pair) per WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 in both the light and dark token sets.

[failure] Given a contrast pair that falls below the applicable threshold, when the test runs, then the failure message names the selector, state, theme, foreground colour, background colour, computed ratio and the threshold applied, and the test exits non-zero so the suite blocks a merge that drops a pair below AA.
US-208 command page suite (query-routes)

[happy] Given a running viewer and a known id, when GET "./trace.json?id=<id>&direction=forward" is requested, then the response is application/json carrying the computeTrace result for that pivot (pivot, direction, found, nodes, edges), computed from the current state and served with "cache-control: no-store" relative to the viewer mount.

[happy] Given a running viewer and a known id, when GET "./impact.json?id=<id>" is requested, then the response is application/json carrying the computeImpact result (pivot, found, nodes with actionNeeded per node, edges) with "cache-control: no-store".

[happy] Given a running viewer, when GET "./coverage.json" is requested with no scope, then the response is application/json carrying the strict computeCoverage result for the whole tree (totals, requirements, unresolvedTestPointers); given "?scope=<id>" naming a PRD, REQ or US, the result is narrowed to that subtree as the CLI positional narrows it.

[failure] Given an unknown id, when trace or impact is requested, then the response is 404 application/json with QueryRouteError.error "unknown-id" and QueryRouteError.id echoing the request; given a direction outside forward, back and both, the response is 400 with QueryRouteError.error "bad-direction"; given a below-AC or unknown scope on coverage, the response is 400 with QueryRouteError.error "bad-scope".

[must-not] Given any request to the three routes, when the server handles it, then runWithAdmissibilityGate is not called (the routes bypass the gate the way src/cli/coverage.js and src/cli/impact.js do) and nothing under rcf/ is written.

[edge] Given a rewalk that publishes a new state.version, when a route is requested, then the served result reflects the new tree and the memo entries of the previous version are discarded; within one version a repeated request for the same pivot and direction is served from the memo without recomputing.
[failure] Given the server before the first walk completes, when a trace, impact or coverage request arrives, then the response is 503 text "view server initialising", as ./index.json answers today.
US-209 command page suite (trace-matrix)

[happy] Given the Trace sub-tab and a pivot id in the hash, when the client fetches "./trace.json" for it, then a matrix renders with one TraceMatrixRow per story and criterion under the pivot and columns for suites, cases, build specs and components, each TraceMatrixCell.reached true where the forward trace reaches the column from the row's criterion.

[happy] Given coverage data for the pivot's criteria, when a cell renders, then TraceMatrixCell.resolution is "resolving" on the --sv-success token, "unresolved" on the --sv-warning token or "none" on the --sv-muted token, with no new colour token introduced.

[happy] Given any id rendered in the questions, blocking, thin-requirements or coverage tables, when the row renders, then it carries a "Trace" action linking to "#tab=readiness&sub=trace&entity=<id>", and a lookup modal hit on a readiness row navigates to the same hash preserving embed and theme.

[edge] Given an SSE tree-update that swaps #rcf-live-content while the Trace sub-tab shows a matrix, when the swap lands, then the matrix is re-rendered from the client cache keyed by state.version and marked stale until the next fetch completes, never dropped.

[must-not] Given the Requirements tab, when a requirement renders, then no Mermaid slice diagram is rendered for it (the per-requirement slice and its details element are gone) and no Mermaid is rendered anywhere on the Readiness tab.
[failure] Given a pivot the route reports with found false, when the Trace sub-tab renders, then an empty state names the id and offers the lookup modal, and no partial matrix is drawn.

[edge] Given a pivot whose forward trace yields more than 200 TraceMatrixRow entries, when the matrix renders, then a row filter by story id or criterion id is shown, the full TraceMatrixRow.cells set is retained in memory and nothing is truncated silently.
the requirement subdiagram is emitted as mermaid flowchart source
each REQ subdiagram carries chain edges REQ to US to AC plus FBS delivery back-links, scoped to that requirement only
every requirement is rendered as its own subdiagram (per-REQ design)
a broken node still renders in the subdiagram and carries the broken class rather than being omitted
Diagram rendering
renderPage renders curated key fields as readable text rather than raw JSON
document links render as anchors targeting the raw doc id section
the rendered page is a valid HTML5 document
the view serves from a local server process and never writes files to disk
style.css nav.tabs has flex-shrink: 0 and no min-width: 0, so the tablist never clips the Build tab under a long project name
style.css .tools has flex-shrink: 0 so the Find button and theme control never shrink into the tablist
style.css .product has min-width: 0 so it yields to the tablist and tools before clipping anything
style.css .product .name has min-width: 0 so text-overflow: ellipsis triggers inside the flex .product
renderPage emits a title="<full name>" attribute on .product .name so hover reveals the whole name under ellipsis
the title attribute shares the escapeHtml path with the inner text so a projectName of "<script>" renders as title="<script>"
no title attribute is emitted when the product block collapses (no projectName)
resolveProductHeader prefers prd.productName over manifest.projectName when both are set
resolveProductHeader falls back to manifest.projectName when the PRD carries no productName
resolveProductHeader falls back to prd.productTitle when neither productName nor manifest is set
the renderPage DOM reflects the flipped precedence; the manifest value does not reach the header slice when prd.productName is set
HTML page rendering
an on-disk edit is present in the regenerated view output
regeneration re-walks the tree fresh and drops all prior-state content
buildDagLayout places every connected FBS in a column whose index equals its longest dependency depth from dependsOnFbsIds; rows inside a column are ordered by buildOrder ascending.

buildDagLayout carries upstream and downstream closures transitively per node; renderBuildDag outlines upstream in link colour and downstream in warning (checked via data-rcf-dag-role on nodes and edges in the client wiring markers).

buildDagInspectorPayload emits status, area, buildOrder, acCount, buildable, needs and waits (direct + transitive totals) plus needsMeta/waitsMeta for every node, so the client inspector lists them without recomputing the layout.

page-init.js carries the Build/DAG wiring: click-to-highlight writes #tab=build&sub=dag&entity=<id>, applyBuildHash restores the selection and scrolls the node into view (auto-pressing Show-unconnected when the restored node sits in the unconnected lane).

DAG filter chips (status, area, Buildable-now, Critical-path, Show-unconnected) in the DagToolbar; applyDagFilters keeps the current selection intact across toggles; renderBuildDag emits the toolbar with the six filter controls and the unconnected count.
buildDagLayout surfaces cycle members as cycleIds and excludes them from the depth layout; non-cycle FBS still render.
The rendered Build tab slice (DAG panel) does not contain any postMessage( call site; the inspector payload rides on a data-rcf-dag-inspector-data attribute, not a function call.
Viewer UI refresh build stream: Build/DAG sub-tab, filters, inspector and later tab deltas (US-204, US-205, US-18002 and successor USs)
rankLookupRows ranks an exact id match first, a prefix match second and a contains match third; the first ranked row is pre-highlighted in the LookupModal shell.
rankLookupRows ranks a word match in the title above a word match in the snippet when the id does not match; every query word must match title or snippet.
rankLookupRows with a one-character query returns only id matches; the title / snippet word-match pass is skipped.
wireLookup pick writes `#tab=<tab>&entity=<id>` through writeHash; the Router activates the tab, opens every ancestor DocRow and the entity, scrolls into view and flashes the target.
A mount URL of `?tab=requirements&entity=US-304` lands on the same position at first paint via the Router (PR 1 contract), independent of the LookupModal.
A pick with `?embed=1&theme=dark` on the URL leaves both query params in place; only the hash fragment changes. Verified against writeHash + the hash-preservation helpers.

A non-2xx / malformed `./index.json` response renders the empty state (The index could not be loaded.) with a visible Reload index button; no result rows show; the reload affordance re-fetches on click.

wireLookup never calls window.postMessage, never writes to localStorage / sessionStorage / document.cookie, and makes no outbound fetch other than `./index.json`; asserted by a source-level scan of page-init.js (no postMessage, no storage, no cookie writes in wireLookup).

The WCAG 2.1 AA contrast audit (test/view/contrast-aa.test.js) requires a `.rcf-search-btn` pair for each of hover, focus-visible and active (state rules merged over the base rule) in both the light and dark token sets and asserts >= 4.5:1 for the button text and >= 3:1 for the focus ring against the surface it sits on. A missing state pair fails the test (PR 291 landing review F3).

renderTestHostPage returns an HTML5 document with a 56px wespa-header, data-rcf-host-sidebar + data-rcf-host-sidebar-drag markers, data-rcf-host-theme light/dark toggles, an iframe whose src is literally './?embed=1&theme=light' (HTML-entity encoded), a '<script src=./test-host.js defer>' line and zero inline <script> blocks.

The router serves /test-host.html with the fixture body (iframe src + script tag) and /test-host.js with application/javascript when testHost: true; both routes return 404 by default so wespa's reverse-proxy allow-list is unaffected.

src/view/test-host/embed-client.js posts { type: 'rcf-view-theme', theme } to iframe.contentWindow targeting window.location.origin, and its code (comments stripped) contains no localStorage/sessionStorage write (ADR-4136 does-not-persist invariant). The live postMessage round-trip is captured in Playwright evidence (agents/dave/remote-lane/inbox/r-20261002-161325-e2a2/output/evidence/test-host-dark-iframe-flipped.png).

src/view/page-init.js exposes writeHash (reassigns location.hash only, preserving the search string by construction) and stamps data-embed + data-theme on load. Live hash-nav proof lives in Playwright evidence (hash-nav-proof.txt + test-host-iframe-hash-nav-embed-preserved.png).

src/view/page-init.js registers an addEventListener('message', ...) whose first guard returns early when ev.origin !== window.location.origin; cross-origin messages never reach the applyTheme path and <html data-theme> is unchanged.

assertFramingHeaders over GET / returns ok: true (no X-Frame-Options; no CSP frame-ancestors forbidding same-origin). Positive + negative unit cases also pass (refuses on X-Frame-Options present, refuses on frame-ancestors 'none', accepts frame-ancestors 'self').

assertNoTargetTop returns count: 0 across every rendered page (renderPage shell, renderComponentsFixturePage, renderTestHostPage). Also lints the populated dogfood tree render (renderModelToPage) so per-document conditional output cannot smuggle a target="_top" past the test. Positive + negative unit cases cover target="_top" / target='_top' / target=_top.
assertLocalStorageNamespace over the src/view tree returns ok: true; every localStorage/sessionStorage call site resolves to a key starting with 'rcf-view:v1:'.
A grep over src/view/** (excluding test-host/embed-client.js, the sanctioned emitter) finds zero .postMessage( call sites; the embed-client itself posts exactly one shape, 'rcf-view-theme'.

renderPage renders a `[data-rcf-theme-control]` group with three buttons (Light, Dark, Auto; `aria-pressed`) right of the SearchButton in `.tools` when `data-embed` is absent; a click on a theme button sets `<html data-theme>` live and flips `aria-pressed` across the three.

In non-embed mode, selecting a theme writes `rcf-view:v1:theme` as `light`/`dark`/`auto` and the stored value is reapplied on the next boot; a `rcf-view-theme` postMessage still applies live but does not write the stored key; the boot precedence is `?theme=` -> stored -> auto.

renderPage with `data-embed="1"` does not emit any `[data-rcf-theme-control]` markup; wireThemeControl under embed never reads or writes `rcf-view:v1:theme` on load, on a postMessage, or on any user action; the key is zero-touched (localStorage spy sees no setItem/getItem call for the key under embed).

In non-embed mode with a stored value `dark`, when the URL carries `?theme=light`, boot resolves to `light` (explicit wins), the Light button is pressed and the stored value is NOT overwritten (next load without a query reuses `dark`).

Boot `?embed=1` with no `?theme=`, post `{ type: "rcf-view-theme", theme: "dark" }`, then call `rcfPage.init()` (the live-client SSE re-run): `<html data-theme>` stays `dark` and no storage is touched.
Boot `?theme=light` in non-embed mode, click Dark, then call `rcfPage.init()`: `<html data-theme>` stays `dark` and the Dark button stays pressed.

The audit parses `src/view/style.css`, enumerates every selector that sets `color` with every reachable background (own rule, ancestor surface token, page background `--sv-canvas`) in each state (default, :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, :active, [aria-pressed=true], [aria-selected=true], .is-active, :disabled) in both the light and dark token sets, computes the WCAG relative-luminance ratio and asserts >= 4.5:1 for normal text and >= 3:1 for large text and non-text UI boundaries (WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11).

When a contrast pair is below the threshold, the test failure message names the selector, state, theme, foreground colour, background colour, computed ratio and applied threshold; the test exits non-zero so the suite blocks a merge that drops below AA.

A state rule that changes only the background (the original `.rcf-search-btn:hover` defect) is merged over its base selector and paired with the inherited colour; `border` / `border-color` and `outline` / `outline-color` are enumerated against the adjacent surface at the 3:1 non-text threshold; run against the pre-amendment stylesheet the helper reports the dark `.rcf-search-btn:hover` failure.
`.rcf-theme-btn` hover, focus-visible and active pairs exist and pass in both themes, and its focus ring clears 3:1 against the surface it sits on.
